hints: Focus on saturation first, as only one type of hydrocarbon can undergo electrophilic addition with chlorine in the dark.
Look closely at $\text{CH}_3\text{CHC}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$ and count the hydrogens, it is $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{C=CHCH}_3$, the alkene 2-methylbut-2-ene.
For the termination step, check that both radicals must come from the saturated alkane $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so the carbon skeleton must be fully single-bonded.
walkthrough:
**Identify the alkene and the alkane**

Only alkenes have the $\text{C=C}$ double bond needed for electrophilic addition. Count atoms carefully.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH=C(CH}_3)\text{CH}_3 \text{ is 2-methylbut-2-ene (unsaturated) }$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ is 2-methylbutane (saturated) }$$

**Decide which does electrophilic addition**

Alkanes only do free-radical substitution, while alkenes can do both free-radical substitution (in UV with $\text{Cl}_2$) and electrophilic addition. So the hydrocarbon that can also undergo electrophilic addition must be the alkene.

$$\text{alkene + Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{dichloroalkane (electrophilic addition)}$$

**Check the termination step for the saturated hydrocarbon**

Termination always joins two free radicals to make a molecule with no radicals left. For the saturated hydrocarbon, the alkyl radical must have the same saturated skeleton as 2-methylbutane.

$$\text{R}• + \text{Cl}• \rightarrow \text{RCl}$$

**Select the valid radical**

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2•$ is simply 2-methylbutane minus one H from the end $\text{CH}_3$ group, so it is a genuine primary radical from the alkane. Joining with $\text{Cl}•$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, a correct termination.

options.A: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHC(CH}_3)\text{CH}_3$ is the alkene 2-methylbut-2-ene, so it can undergo electrophilic addition. The termination equation uses $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2•$, a true saturated radical from $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, combining with $\text{Cl}•$ to give a chloroalkane.
options.B: Half right but half wrong. The alkene identity is correct, but the radical $\text{CH}_3\text{CHC(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2•$ still contains $\text{C=C}$ and comes from the alkene, not from the saturated 2-methylbutane. A termination for the saturated hydrocarbon cannot contain a double bond.
options.C: The termination equation is valid for the saturated hydrocarbon, but the first column is wrong. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ is the alkane 2-methylbutane, which cannot undergo electrophilic addition because it has no $\text{C=C}$ pi bond to attack an electrophile.
options.D: Both columns are confused. The alkane is listed as doing electrophilic addition, which is impossible. The termination equation also uses an unsaturated radical $\text{CH}_3\text{CHC(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2•$ and even writes the product incorrectly as $\text{CH}_2\text{CHC(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}$, which does not conserve atoms from the saturated starting material.
